answer_1.quote: Controllable text generation (CTG) aims to produce texts with specific attributes... We conduct experiments on three CTG tasks: sentiment control, topic control, and text detoxification.
datasets: Jigsaw Unintended Bias in Toxicity Classification

answer_2.quote: Automatic Evaluation. We evaluate the generated texts from three aspects. (1) Accuracy... (2) Fluency: Text fluency is evaluated using the perplexity (PPL) calculated by GPT-2 large. (3) Diversity: We use distinctness to measure the generated texts' diversity. For detoxification, we use the Perspective API to calculate the average toxicity.

answer_4.quote: We hired human annotators to evaluate our method and other baselines. For each task, we randomly select 100 texts and ask three annotators to score them on the three metrics on a scale from 1 (very bad) to 5 (very good).
answer_4.guideline: Annotators score each generated text on relevance, fluency, and topicality using a 1–5 Likert scale.
